title: Tokenized KV Mosaic Allocation and Anti-Fragmentation Guidelines
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Introduce a new KV cache allocation strategy ("tokenized mosaic") and an operational anti-fragmentation system that ties live compaction to continuous-batching boundaries. Goal: reduce GPU-side fragmentation and tail latency for models with high token churn, without sacrificing throughput from continuous batching. This ticket designs the approach, implements a reference controller, and prepares rollout/telemetry for runtime-1.22.
acceptance_criteria: New allocation controller can be deployed behind remote flag and reduce measured fragmentation score by >=25% on production-like traces
No regression in median generation latency (>5ms) and 95th percentile tail latency not worse than 10% relative to baseline under load
Operational metrics: compaction run duration, compaction-related GPU stall time, and token relocation rate exposed in Console dashboards
Canary rollout plan documented and automated job for simulated workload validation included
notes: 2025-02-18: Kickoff sync with runtime and infra teams. We agreed to favor non-blocking background relocation over synchronous compaction during hot paths. 2025-02-25: Initial simulator results show tokenized mosaics reduce small free-slot fragmentation but increase relocation events by ~12% under bursty access patterns. 2025-03-03: Design review with PM and Observability; added compaction score metric and tracing spans for relocation operations. 2025-03-07: Implemented baseline controller in branch 'kv/mosaic-controller' and smoke-tested on dedicated staging pool.
design_decisions: 1) Allocation units are 'mosaic segments' sized to token access distribution percentiles (P25,P50,P90). 2) Hot token pins: tokens above hotness threshold are mapped to pinned micro-segments to avoid churn. 3) Background compaction runs aligned to continuous-batching 'safe windows' to avoid interfering with request-critical KV hotspots. 4) Use probabilistic relocation with capped budget rather than immediate eviction to smooth GPU memory pressure. 5) Make per-model heuristics configurable via model_profile configs rather than hard-coded thresholds.
technical_approach: Phase A: analytics and simulator. Collect token-access histograms, fragmentation profiles, and batch boundary timestamps. Phase B: implement mosaic allocator that picks a segment size per token cohort and places new KV entries into least-fragmented mosaic. Phase C: implement compaction controller with three lanes: opportunistic (micro), scheduled (windowed during low batch activity), and emergency (hard reclaim). Background relocations are preemptible and report spans. Integrate backpressure signals from request router to throttle relocation during high-latency windows. Provide metrics: fragmentation_score, relocation_rate, pinned_ratio, compaction_time, compaction_stall_ms.
